waivers.scope: .claude/skills/code-map/scripts/code_index/code_index.py — the flat imports compiled_index, graph_metrics, map_render, py_index, ts_index
waivers.reason: False positive on vendored harness code. All five names are sibling modules in the same directory (compiled_index.py, graph_metrics.py, map_render.py, py_index.py, ts_index.py all exist next to code_index.py). code_index.py runs as a standalone script with its own directory on sys.path, so the imports are flat rather than relative — the sensor reads them as unresolvable third-party pypi packages. Verified by directory listing before waiving. Not fixed by rewriting to relative imports, because that would break standalone execution of a harness control-plane script this project does not own.

waivers.scope: frontend/eslint.config.js and frontend/vite.config.ts (frontend build/lint tooling), plus backend/src/__init__.py and backend/tests/__init__.py (package markers)
waivers.reason: component-map.md lists component files only, with no row for build/lint tooling or package markers. eslint.config.js and vite.config.ts are required by ESLint 9's flat-config default and by Vite; neither carries business behavior. The two __init__.py files are 0-byte package markers that anchor `src` and `tests` as importable packages -- the /gate reviewer proposed deleting them as inconsistent with the namespace-package style used by the subpackages, and that was tried and reverted: removing them breaks every import (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src'), so they are load-bearing rather than leftovers. Adding all four to component-map.md would mean a third design-receipt re-record in one session for files that are tooling, not components. RATIFIED by ovi-rosu 2026-09-14. Note run-gate-checks.js has no waiver-application path -- waivers apply at pre-commit only -- so that runner will keep reporting ownership-check as blocked; discount it there.

waivers.scope: One commit only: the E15-S1 test-file split (backend/tests/unit/test_log_redaction.py 16 -> 9 test defs)
waivers.reason: Relocation, not deletion. The guard counts test definitions per file, so a file split reads as lost coverage. The 7 moved blocks were transplanted verbatim into three new files that component-map.md now lists for E15-S1: test_correlation_id.py (5), test_error_envelope.py (3) and test_health_probe.py (1). Verified: 9+5+3+1 = 18 test definitions across the four files versus 16 in the one before, and pytest --collect-only reports 77 tests collected versus 73 before the change, so total coverage rose rather than fell. No assertion was weakened and nothing was skipped. The split was forced by the 500-line hard limit, which pre-write-gate applied correctly to a 519-line file carrying six responsibilities. Expires in two days: this covers one commit and must not shelter a later real deletion.

waivers.scope: Group A remediation commits only: the 4 remaining findings are group B's api_checks (QA-VM-012 through QA-VM-015)
waivers.reason: Scoping artifact, not a regression. The gate grades every sprint contract rather than the group in flight -- the same flaw /gate itself recorded when regression-suite-full graded 12 unbuilt groups against a dead server. Verified directly: with no server listening it reported 7 findings, all 'got 0' (no HTTP response at all). With uvicorn up on the configured port it reports 4, and group A's QA-VM-003/004/005 PASS and drop off the list entirely. The 4 that remain are group B's endpoints returning 404 because E1-S1 has not been implemented yet -- an unbuilt group cannot satisfy its contract, and that is the plan working, not a defect. Expires in two days: it covers the group A remediation commits and must not shelter a real regression once group B lands.
